thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: kv-cache continuous-batching error rate spike detected (10m window). routing: hosted-us-west, affected-pools: gpu-pool-3. severity: P1. paging oncall.
alex wang: seeing frontend 95p latency jump from 120ms -> 900ms, and a bunch of streaming disconnects. trace IDs in logs point to kv cache misses + aborts during speculative decode path.
maria gonzalez: confirmed, synthetic traffic shows batch size oscillation: sudden jumps to 512 then collapse. CPU on pool instances climbs and we start dropping requests.
jamie: customer-reported impact: 3 enterprise tenants on dedicated saw higher costs due to replays; one reported partial API errors for chat streaming.
prateek: initial graph: kv-cache size exploded, lots of draft keys never replaced, cache-eviction didn't kick in because of a TTL bug with speculative draft tagging.
oncall: paging ack. I'm on it, will gather logs and set mitigations. tagging @sre-lead for visibility.
sre-lead: good. first priority: stop customer impact. second: find root cause (speculative decode interaction with kv batching).
ops-bot: current alarms: kv_cache_size > 95% (gpu-pool-3) ; batch_cliff_rate > 8% ; spec_decode_mismatch_rate > 4%. Autoscaler paused: false.
alex wang: quick mitigation proposal: 1) disable speculative decoding on host pools (env flag) 2) throttle batch size to 32 3) force kv-cache prefix eviction for speculative drafts. low risk and fast.
maria gonzalez: agree. disabling speculative decode should reduce draft churn. how fast can we flip the flag in hosted? it's a config roll, 2-3 min.
prateek: I can push a hotfix for kv-cache eviction policy to drop keys tagged "spec-draft" older than 30s. patch ready but needs canary.
jamie: customers want immediate fix. do we have rollback plan if eviction causes regressions?
alex wang: rollback = re-enable old TTL + revert config. I'll create feature flag so we can toggle at region level.
oncall: I'm going to set temporary ingress throttles to reduce request rate by 30% for gpu-pool-3. applying now.
ops-bot: command executed: curl -X POST https://infra/api/throttle -d '{"pool":"gpu-pool-3","reduce_pct":30}' -> 202 ACCEPTED
maria gonzalez: throttle in. latency dropped to ~240ms 95p, errors reduced but still elevated compared to baseline.
prateek: starting canary for eviction patch in pool-3-canary (1 instance). deployment command:

kubectl -n inference set image deploy/kv-cache kv-cache=kv-cache:evict-spec-0.1-canary

prateek: monitoring canary logs: eviction loop triggered and removed ~8k stale keys in first minute.
alex wang: good. any client-facing incidents to open? Jamie, do you want me to draft customer notes?
jamie: yes please. say: "we're investigating increased latencies and intermittent streaming failures due to internal cache behavior; temporary mitigations applied; no data loss". avoid deep technicals.
sre-lead: once canary stable for 5m, roll to remaining pool-3 nodes. if evictions cause misses causing more load, be ready to roll back quickly.
prateek: canary stable at 6m. rolling to rest of pool-3 now. rollout command in parallel with batch-size cap:

infractl rollout kv-cache --selector pool=gpu-pool-3 --image kv-cache:evict-spec-0.1
infractl set-config inference.batch.max_size=32 --scope pool=gpu-pool-3

ops-bot: rollout started, set-config succeeded.
alex wang: after full roll, 95p latency back to ~130ms, error rate near baseline. cost per token for affected tenants reduced by ~12% compared to spike window.
maria gonzalez: we still see occasional batch size spikes when there is a burst of short requests combined with speculative drafts. need long term fix: align draft/target key tagging so speculative drafts don't bypass eviction TTL.
jamie: customers notified (sent initial note). one enterprise replied asking for timeline for root cause and permanent fix.
prateek: investigative notes: root cause hypothesis: speculative decode flow was creating transient draft keys with tag "no-evict" due to a flag typo introduced in prior release. combined with continuous batching heuristics, these drafts accumulated and overwhelmed prefix eviction heuristics, leading to batch amplification and perf cliffs.
alex wang: reproduced locally with stress test: sequence: many short requests + speculative enabled -> per-request KV insert rate spikes -> evictions fail -> batch size growth -> OOM/abort.
sre-lead: good repro. next steps: create a patch to fix the flag and add a safety TTL for speculative-draft keys at render-time. also add metric guardrails: reject batch size > 128 and a slow-path that forces immediate eviction when cache-growth-rate > threshold.
oncall: handing off to daytime oncall shift. summary for next oncall:
- what happened: speculative decoding bug left draft keys non-evictable, continuous-batching amplified requests causing cache blowup and latency/errors.
- immediate mitigations applied: ingress throttle (30%), disabled speculative decode flag regionally, kv-cache eviction hotfix deployed (evicted stale spec-drafts), batch max_size cap to 32.
- status now: stable. 95p latency ~130ms, errors back to baseline. no customer data lost. awaiting permanent fix PR and postmortem.
- actions for next oncall: monitor kv_cache_size, spec_decode_mismatch_rate, batch_cliff_rate; be prepared to rollback kv-cache evict patch if unexpected errors; coordinate with release team for a config-safe rollout.
sre-lead: assign owners: prateek -> root-cause patch + tests; maria -> add metric guardrails + dashboards; alex -> customer comms and rollback plan; jamie -> coordinate postmortem and customer follow-ups.
ops-bot: created ticket INF-4321 in incidents board, linked runbook snippets and graphs.
jamie: I'll schedule a postmortem meeting in 24h, invite eng/ops/product/SO team reps. draft incident note will go out in 2h after we collect more metrics.
alex wang: quick note for postmortem: include synthetic workload that exposed the issue (short-chat pattern + high speculative ratio). ops: please save heapdumps for two affected instances.
oncall: handing off complete. tagging next oncall: @alex wang (day shift). please ack.
alex wang: ack. I'll monitor for 2 hours then hand back.
sre-lead: closing incident channel for now but keep it open for updates. good job everyone. :tada:
